Clinical quality in postoperative care is evaluated using specific national metrics, including [[indikator-5|Indikator 5]], which focuses on the monitoring of high-risk surgical patients. In [[danmark|Danmark]], this indicator assesses the proportion of patients with elevated mortality risk who receive extended postoperative observation. Current data shows that the proportion of high-risk patients (defined as ASA ≥ 3 or age ≥ 75 years) monitored for at least 24 hours postoperatively in an intermediate or similar unit is 22.9% (95% CI: 21.1–24.8) [^src1]. This figure provides a specific benchmark for evaluating clinical quality and patient safety protocols for vulnerable demographics across the country.

## Claims
- Andelen af patienter med høj mortalitetsrisiko (ASA ≥ 3 eller alder ≥ 75 år), der monitoreres ≥ 24 timer postoperativt på et intermediært eller lignende afsnit, er 22,9 % (95 % CI: 21,1–24,8) [^src1] (indikator-5, danmark)
